description: Orbital Pulse brings together AI, robust backend architectures, and intelligent data systems into one focused 4-member team. We’re here to take a bold idea from concept to a live demo. Roster full, ready to ship!
summary:
Orbital Pulse is an autonomous deep-space astronaut health monitoring system built for missions like Mars, where a 4-to-24-minute communication delay eliminates real-time telemedicine. Instead of trusting a single sensor or unconstrained AI, every check-in passes through an Input Integrity Gate and three blind, isolated assessment pipelines—personal statistical baselines (NASA OSDR Inspiration4), explicit physiological limits (ISS ALTEA/RadLab & DONKI space weather), and a caged, offline local LLM that can flag anomalies but never downgrade risk or prescribe doses.

A deterministic Checker referee selects the most cautious verdict, maps it to six whitelisted actions, and records every decision in an HMAC-signed, hash-chained flight log that Earth can replay byte-for-byte. To prevent cognitive overload during emergencies, Orbital Pulse delivers verdicts through a hands-free, gesture-controlled Augmented Reality Visor HUD alongside a Crew Habitat Tablet and Earth Oversight Console. It is decision support the crew can trust immediately and Mission Control can audit later.
details:
What It Does and How It Works: Orbital Pulse is an offline decision support engine, not a diagnostic tool, built so an astronaut can trust what the screen says when Earth is up to 22 minutes away. Every check in runs through a pure,deterministic decide() pipeline:

Input Gate: Rejects stale (over 1 hour old), contradictory, wrong unit, stuck sensor, or unverified readings before anything interprets them.

Three Blind Parallel Pipelines: Isolated assessors that never see each other's output. Pipeline A tracks statistical drift against personal Inspiration4 baselines using CUSUM. Pipeline B checks explicit clinical threshold limits. Pipeline D is an optional, loopback only local Ollama LLM that can raise a tier, never lower one, never name a dose or drug, and fails a grounding check if it invents data.

Deterministic Checker Referee: Picks the most cautious verdict across GREEN, YELLOW, RED, and GREY (where unverified data is treated as urgent, never as all clear) and maps it to six whitelisted actions.

Tamper Evident Flight Recorder and Three Zero Intelligence Views: Every decision is bundled into an HMAC signed,hash chained record. Plain HTML and JS views (Helmet HUD with NASA STD 3001 rules and point and pinch EVA gestures, Crew Health Monitor, and read only Earth Base) strictly display backend verdicts and show an explicit NO LINK state rather than stale data.

Benefits and Intended Impact Across a 22 minute Mars light delay, Mission Control cannot step in during an emergency.Orbital Pulse calculates delay aware autonomy for every alert, logging GROUND_IN_LOOP near the Moon (where the crew owns 0 of 3 alerts alone) versus ONBOARD_AUTHORITY at far Mars (where the crew owns 3 of 3 alone). At the same time, Earth can replay any decision byte for byte, verify signed checkpoints, and test proposed rule changes against past decisions before uplinking them.

Tools, Languages and Hardware Used Backend and Evidence Engine: Python, pytest (557 passing tests), deterministic rule policy (policy.yaml), HMAC signed hash chains, and optional local Ollama inference running loopback only.Frontend and Interface Proxy: Plain HTML and JS served at /ui/, using a webcam and point and pinch hand tracking to stand in for future suit integrated AR helmet optics. NASA Open Data: NASA OSDR Inspiration4 (OSD 569, OSD 575) for personal glucose and blood baselines, NASA OSDR RadLab (DosTel, CRaTER, BPD, MSL RAD, ISS ALTEA) for radiation dose validation, and CCMC DONKI for the May 2024 solar storm timeline.

How It Is Creative Instead of wrapping vitals in an unconstrained chatbot, we enforce architectural honesty. Our views contain zero medical logic, every reading on screen is explicitly labeled REAL (with its dataset ID) or SIMULATED, and the local LLM is strictly caged. An automated red team suite of 18 adversarial attacks (stale data, stuck sensors, forged NASA provenance, an LLM suggesting a dose, killed pipelines, and tampered or truncated history) runs against the real backend with 18 of 18 blocked and 0 unsafe approvals, compared to 4 to 10 unsafe approvals in stripped down ablation variants.

Factors Considered, Honest Limits and AI Use Declaration Honest Limits: Clinical thresholds are declared project defined placeholders awaiting medical review, and our validation run openly reports that the placeholder radiation rule flags 31% of quiet ISS samples. The onboard LLM has not yet been tested against a live local model, signing uses one shared HMAC key, and the API has no authentication yet. AI Use Declaration: AI coding tools were used to help write code,tests, and documentation in this repository. Our team reviewed and ran all code, and every reported metric comes from real runs of our evidence suite (seed 42) or CI. No NASA logos, flags, or mission identifiers are used or modified, and no AI generated images are included.
